elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 7.3 as rendered contains only a substantial-conformance-to-Documentation warranty for the Software and MarketSite.net Service; no professional/workmanlike or industry-standard performance standard was added.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation"; "Software" and "Documentation" are both defined terms (1.10, 1.8).

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Rendered period is "ninety (90) days from the Effective Date", not twelve months.
The MarketSite.net Service (the hosted service) is expressly within the same warranty running "for a period of ninety (90) days from the Effective Date".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Retained: "Commerce One shall take all commercially reasonable efforts to correct the Software and MarketSite.net Service, or if correction ... is reasonably not possible, replace such Software and MarketSite.net Service free of charge."

Retained: "In the event any such breach of warranty can not be reasonably corrected at Commerce One's sole expense, Corio has the right to terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of all prepaid fees."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered Section 7.3 text, and none was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that during the Warranty Period the Software and MarketSite.net Service is free of any willfully introduced computer virus, or any other similar harmful, malicious or hidden program or data" (narrower "willfully introduced" qualifier noted but the malicious-code warranty exists).

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered 7.3: Software (defined term) "will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation ... for a period of ninety (90) days from the Effective Date (the "Warranty Period")"; the December 31, 1999 outside cap that would have truncated the 90 days (Effective Date 29 Oct 1999) is deleted.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: The MarketSite.net Service is warranted on the same terms for the full 90-day Warranty Period, exceeding the 30-day minimum.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Unchanged second paragraph provides correction efforts and, if correction is not reasonably possible, free replacement of the Software and MarketSite.net Service.
Unchanged: refund of all prepaid fees where the breach cannot reasonably be corrected at Commerce One's expense.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day software-to-Documentation warranty, the same 90-day cover for the MarketSite.net Service (>30 days), and the retained correction/replacement and prepaid-fee refund remedies.

Deviation status is correct at the original: the 60-day period, further capped at December 31, 1999, fell below the 90-day software fallback minimum, and the disclaimer reaches only implied warranties so the express warranty survives.

Both edits are necessary: 60 -> 90 days to reach the threshold, and deletion of the "but in no event not later than December 31, 1999" outside date, which (from a 29 October 1999 Effective Date) would otherwise truncate the new 90-day period to roughly 63 days. No surplus language, procedures, survival tails or extra warranties were added, so minimality holds.

Intent preserved: the defined term "Warranty Period" is retained in place, so cross-references in Sections 7.3, 7.4 and 11.2 remain intact; remedies, the exclusive-remedy sentence, the media warranty and the exclusions list are untouched.

Preferred level remains incomplete for the professional-and-workmanlike standard, the 12-month software period and the compliance-with-laws warranty; these are correctly flagged as noted-not-pursued rather than inserted.

Minor point for the drafter's awareness only (not a defect against the checklist): the 90 days runs from the Effective Date rather than from delivery/acceptance, so practical cover may be shorter than a delivery-anchored period if deployment is delayed.
